cards.q: What is link redundancy and what options provide it?
cards.a: Link redundancy protects against link failure using multiple parallel physical links. Options include EtherChannel (bundling links into one logical LAG), link aggregation, and multichassis LAG (M-LAG). Bundling kills STP blocking and spreads load.

It bundles multiple physical links into one logical link (port-channel), raises bandwidth, provides availability with no single point of failure, shares load via a hash that picks a member link, and auto-redirects on member failure. Only the LAG, not individual links, is blocked by STP.

cards.q: What protocols negotiate an EtherChannel and their modes?
cards.a: LACP (IEEE 802.3ad/802.1AX) is the standard with active/passive modes, PAgP is Cisco-proprietary with desirable/auto modes, and static configuration uses mode on with no negotiation.

cards.q: How does EtherChannel load balancing work?
cards.a: A hash selects a member link per flow: src/dst MAC for L2 hashing, src/dst IP for L3, src/dst port for L4, or a mix for full flow. Hashing keeps all packets of a single flow in order on one member.
A multichassis LAG (generic term) or vPC (NX-OS) that lets two switches share one logical bundle, running active-active on both, and is used for double-homed servers on access.

cards.q: What commands configure and verify an EtherChannel?
cards.a: Create interface Port-channel1, then bind member interfaces with channel-group 1 mode active (or mode on for static). Verify with show etherchannel summary and show etherchannel load-balance.

cards.q: What is the difference between LACP, PAgP, and static EtherChannel?
cards.a: LACP is the IEEE standard and uses active/passive modes; PAgP is Cisco-proprietary using desirable/auto; mode on is static with no negotiation. Members must have consistent speed/duplex, and the hash keeps a single flow in order on one member so vPC/M-LAG is active-active across two switches.

cards.q: What are common EtherChannel failure symptoms and their checks?
cards.a: Not bundled points to a mode mismatch (check summary), flapping points to speed/duplex mismatch (check config), one-directional behavior points to protocol (check peers), wrong hash points to algorithm (check config), and STP blocking indicates it is not a real LAG (check ports).

cards.q: What is the bundle, standard, and failure behavior for link redundancy?
cards.a: The bundle is an EtherChannel, the standard is LACP (mode active/passive), Cisco's PAgP uses desirable/auto, static is mode on, the logical unit is a port-channel, a hash maps a flow to a member, M-LAG is vPC, and on failure remaining members auto-redirect.
